svg.title: A common finite-capacity region and uniform integer rounding
svg.desc: Finite central units transfer to finite larger-center units. The maximal finite region is common, and bounded truncations prove equality of capacities. The final bar uses theta five halves, trace weight two fifths and matrix size three; its exact removed trace is one fifth.
svg.text: The common finite-capacity region
Actual N ⊂ M; canonical A ⊂ B; physical centers U, V and W = U ∩ V.
A. Transfer finite units, then compare the maximal regions — 86.1–86.6
I(ẑ) = Σ aᵢ ẑ aᵢ*, a₁ = 1
r̂ = support I(ẑ) ∈ Z(B)
ẑ ≤ r̂ ≤ I(ẑ); Tr(r̂) ≤ dt
maximal fA ≤ maximal fB
The individual r need not be common.
Reverse: y = E_A(r̂) is positive central, integrable; finite spectral cuts cover its support.
E_A(r̂(1 − f̂A)) = 0; faithfulness gives r̂ ≤ f̂A.
Thus f̂A = f̂B and fA = fB = f ∈ W.
Every nonzero finite represented central unit has trace ≥ 1 (85.1).
Hats denote represented operators; physical labels are identified by the full Jones corner.
B. Infinite total trace is allowed — bounded truncations carry the proof
K_B = E_V(K_A); on f, K_A = E_U(κ K_B). Therefore T(K_A f) = K_A f.
For a = K_A f and a_L = min(a, Lf): T(a_L) ≤ a_L, and both bounded integrals agree.
Faithfulness gives T(a_L) = a_L; 83.3 gives a_L ∈ W. Let L increase.
K_A = K_B = K, affiliated with W
w_j = 1{K ≤ j} ∈ W; Tr(ŵ_j) ≤ j
K = ∞ on 1 − f; finite cuts w_j ↑ f.
Diagnostic: m_j = 2⁻ʲ, K(j) = 2ʲ
Each atom has unit trace 1; total trace = ∞.
A probability example; no actual core construction.
On each nonzero w_j: a normal compatible trace state has density Kw_j / Tr(ŵ_j).
It gives fv = fb = 0 for the joint discrepancy and canonical positive cost (86.11–86.12).
C. Round a common finite block; control every ambient unitary — 86.13–86.14
Choose a common atom z ≤ w_j. Example arithmetic: θ = 5/2, τ(z) = 2/5, n = 3.
New dimension = n²θ = 45/2; k = 22; removed dimension r_n = 1/2.
Unit p = ẑ commutes with every u ∈ M. Prescribe q ≤ p with dimension kz.
retained q: dimension 22
removed: dimension 1/2
retained trace = 44/5
removed trace = 1/5
Widths: 20 pixels per dimension unit; height: 80 × τ(z) = 32 pixels.
δ_u(q) ≤ 2√(r_n/k) = 1/√11 in this arithmetic; choose k > 4/ε² in general.
One integer and one projection work for every ambient unitary. No amenability input is used.
Scope: finite-capacity rounding is complete when f ≠ 0; the residual case has K_A = K_B = ∞.
Nonzero support does not prove near-one common BF, exact full partition or unrestricted generation.
Proof locators: 86.1–86.14; exact providers 52, 68, 83 and 85. Bars encode dimension and trace.
Human context: Popa 1994, Theorem 4.2.2, printed pp.213–214. Reproducible schematic; no 3D geometry.
